chapter.intro: Intro: The Man With Many Faces
introI.title: The Man With Many Faces
introI.1: Three days from now, in Ironhaven, the city of iron and snow.
introI.2: A man who has been many people wakes in a cell, with nobody's face but his own.
line.i.plateLook: A dented tin plate. Shiny where the dent is, like a smile. I like it already.
line.i.crustLook: Yesterday's bread. Today it's a brick. Tomorrow, if I'm lucky, it's somebody's cheek.
line.i.nailLook: A bent nail. A poor key, but a very good friend.
line.i.stripLook: A strip torn from the blanket. Long enough to reach a table.
line.i.frameLook: Nessa's frame. Brass ribs, little hinges at the jaw. Put a face on it and the face talks. Better than most faces.
line.i.plasterLook: Flakes of damp plaster. Dry, they crumble. Wet, they set.
line.i.wetPlasterLook: Plaster gone soft in bucket water. It wants something to hold it together.
line.i.puttyLook: Grey putty. It smells faintly of bread and despair. Perfect for a sergeant.
line.i.maskHarrowLook: Sergeant Harrow. Heavy jaw, sad little eyes, my eyebrows. In candlelight, he'd fool his own mother. Poor woman.
line.i.keysLook: Benn's key ring. He won't miss it until he needs it.
line.i.hoodLook: A clerk's hood, ink on the cuffs. Nobody looks under a clerk's hood.
line.i.ledgerLook: The tally ledger. A clerk carrying a ledger is invisible.
line.i.maskClerkLook: Hood and ledger. Not a mask, a posture: shoulders down, eyes on the numbers.
line.i.heroLook: Silas. Thin, clever, wanted in four towns, adored in none. Currently a prisoner. That part's temporary.
line.i.heroLookHarrow: Sergeant Harrow, as far as anyone in this light can tell. I have his frown down perfectly.
line.i.heroLookClerk: A tally clerk. Grey, harmless, forgettable. My favourite person to be.
line.i.heroTalk: Talking to myself again. I'm the only one who laughs at my jokes. Ha. See?
line.i.heroItem: I'm not wearing that. I have standards. Low ones, but standards.
line.i.maskHarrowOn: Evening, Sergeant. I settle him on the frame and the jaw moves when mine does. Do try to look stern.
line.i.maskHarrowOff: Thank you, Sergeant. Dismissed. Silas again, sadly.
line.i.maskClerkOn: Hood up, ledger under my arm, shoulders down. Nobody worth a second look. Bliss.
line.i.maskClerkOff: I push the hood back. Hello again, me.
line.i.harrowCracked: Poor Harrow. He cracked under pressure. They always do.
line.i.wake1: Damp stone. A cold that gets into the teeth. And only one face: mine. Dreadful. Who chose this one?
line.i.wake2: One candle out past the bars, and somebody snoring a little tune beside it. Flat, but heartfelt.
line.i.plateTake: Supper, served on a plate with a dent like a dimple. I shall call her Moonface.
line.i.windowLook: A barred window, high up. A thread of moonlight creeps in and lies down on the floor. Tired, poor thing.
line.i.windowLookLit: Moonface sits wedged in the bars, throwing the moon about like confetti. She's happy there. She stays.
line.i.windowUse: Too high and too small. Even for me, and I've been through smaller.
line.i.angle1: Up you go, Moonface. Wedged between the bars, tilted just so, and catch... the... moon...
line.i.angle2: Ta-da! The whole cell, silver and dripping. Hold the applause.
line.i.angle3: A cot, a bucket, a wall that weeps. And out there, on the guard's table: my frame. Hello, darling.
line.i.cotLook: Straw, and a blanket that has given up on life. I know the feeling. Briefly.
line.i.nailTake: One of the cot's nails was already loose. I bent it a bit more. Now it's interesting.
line.i.stripTake: I tear a long strip from the blanket. It wasn't keeping anyone warm. It may as well be useful.
line.i.cotEmpty: The cot has given me everything. I'll write to it.
line.i.wallLook: The wall weeps. I'd weep too, living here. Its plaster comes away in wet, grey flakes.
line.i.plasterTake: A handful of plaster. Sorry, wall. It's for art.
line.i.bucketLook: A bucket of water. I've decided to believe it's water. Belief is half of everything.
line.i.bucketUse: I'm not that thirsty. Not yet.
line.i.wetPlaster: I soak the plaster. It goes soft and grey and willing, like a clerk on a Friday.
line.i.soggyBread: Soggy bread is still bread. But it wants a partner first.
line.i.putty: Plaster, kneaded into bread. Squish. Squish. A putty that holds a shape. Whose shape? Ooh.
line.i.needFace: The putty is ready, but it has no face in mind. I need someone to copy. Someone stern.
line.i.plasterDry: Dry plaster crumbles if you so much as look at it. It needs water, and something to hold it together.
line.i.harrowMade1: A brow, a jaw, the pouches under the eyes... and a pinch of my own hair for his eyebrows. Hold still, Sergeant.
line.i.harrowMade2: Sergeant Harrow, on Nessa's frame. Not my finest work. He'll still do.
line.i.candleLook: A stub of candle on the guard's table. The only warm thing down here.
line.i.candleTake: It's on the far side of the bars.
line.i.tableLookDark: A table by the candle. Something on it glints.
line.i.tableLook: The guard's table: the candle, a cup, and my mask frame, confiscated. Rude. Just out of reach. Ruder.
line.i.tableLookEmpty: The candle and a cup. The interesting thing is in my satchel now.
line.i.outOfReach: My arms are long. Not that long. I've asked them.
line.i.frameReach: An arm's length and a bit beyond the bars. I need a longer arm. Or a cleverer one.
line.i.fish1: Through the bars, slowly. Past the candle. Don't wake the baby...
line.i.fish2: Nibble, nibble... the nail catches a brass rib...
line.i.fish3: Got it! Nessa's frame, back where it belongs. The strip stays snagged on the table, as a souvenir; the nail I keep.
line.i.roster1: The duty roster. Nights: Benn, cells. Kell, guardroom. Sergeant Harrow, in charge.
line.i.roster2: And someone has doodled Harrow in the margin: heavy jaw, pouched eyes, a moustache like a broom. Hello, handsome. You'll do.
line.i.rosterAgain: Harrow: jaw, pouches, broom. I've got him memorised. I could hum him.
line.i.cellDoorLook: The cell door. A good lock on a bad hinge. We'll talk, the lock and I.
line.i.cellDoorLocked: Locked. Of course. It's always locked. One day a door will just open and I'll faint.
line.i.notWatched: Not while he's sitting right there. Even asleep, that's just bad manners.
line.i.pick1: Nail in the lock. Tickle the pins... one... two... come on, I'm charming...
line.i.doorOpen: The door swings open. Thank you. You're a credit to doors.
line.i.stairsLook: Stairs up, past the guard's chair.
line.i.barsFirst: The bars are in the way.
line.i.guardMumble: ...sorry, Sergeant Harrow... won't happen again... don't tell the captain...
line.i.readGuard1: He's apologising in his sleep. To his sergeant first, and the captain frightens him even more. Sweet boy.
line.i.readGuard2: Cold to the bone and dead tired. A man like that does whatever his sergeant says, especially if it gets him warm.
line.i.readGuardAgain: Afraid of Harrow, more afraid of the captain, and frozen. Everything I need.
line.i.guardLookDark: A shape slumped in a chair by the candle. Snoring.
line.i.guardLook: A young guard asleep on his chair, chin on his chest, shivering in his sleep. A key ring hangs at his belt.
line.i.shout2: Oi! Prisoner here! Needing things! Mostly a door!
line.i.shout3: He'd sleep through a war. He won't wake for a prisoner. For his sergeant, though... oh, I have an idea. I love my ideas.
line.i.noShout: Shouting as myself gets me nothing but snores. Myself is not very persuasive.
line.i.guardItem: He's asleep, and on the far side of the bars.
line.i.afterGuard: Off he goes, up the stairs. Harrow's face cracked as it dried. Goodbye, Sergeant. Now, the lock.
line.i.afterGuardKeys: Off he goes, and his keys stayed with me. They must like me better. Harrow cracked, poor man. He served.
line.i.caught.guard: Wait... your moustache doesn't move when you talk. You're... you're the prisoner! GUARDS!
line.i.caught.think.guard: ...is how it would go, if I played it like that. No, no, no. Again. Slower. What did he mumble in his sleep?
line.i.caught.think.warden: ...and that's the version where I go back to my cell. Rewind. What does Kell want?
line.i.warden1: A guardroom, warm from the stove. And a guard who is very, very awake. Rude.
line.i.warden2: He'll know the real Harrow. Harrow won't survive a second look up here. Sergeant, you're relieved.
line.i.hoodTake: The clerk's hood. It smells of ink and quiet resignation. My size exactly.
line.i.ledgerLook1: Columns of numbers: bread, coal, candles, prisoners.
line.i.ledgerLook2: And in the back, a page of debts. Kell owes the quartermaster for dice.
line.i.ledgerTake: The ledger. A man with a ledger is a man with a reason to be anywhere. I've always wanted a reason.
line.i.clerkMade: Hood up, ledger to the chest, shoulders down, sigh. Not a mask: a posture. I've become boring. It's thrilling.
line.i.stoveLook: The stove. Benn will be very happy next to it, wherever he's got to.
line.i.noGoingBack: I've seen downstairs. One star. Would not stay again.
line.i.grateLook: An iron grate, and the night beyond it. The lock is old.
line.i.keysWrong: None of Benn's keys fit. The grate's on Harrow's ring.
line.i.pick2: Old lock, cold fingers. Shh, shh, it's only me...
line.i.grateOpen: The grate swings open onto the snow. Freedom smells of frost. And a little of drains.
line.i.readWarden1: Kell. Awake, but not by choice: he keeps looking at the clock, and at the kitchen door.
line.i.readWarden2: Hungry. Bored. And he flinches whenever anyone mentions the quartermaster.
line.i.readWarden3: And a man who owes the quartermaster won't argue with the quartermaster's clerk. Hello, clerk. That's me.
line.i.readWardenAgain: Hungry, bored, in debt. Three handles.
line.i.wardenLook: Broad, awake, and the type who'd know his own sergeant's face anywhere.
line.i.wardenLookBusy: Kell's in the kitchen doorway, chewing.
line.i.notHarrowHere: Not with Harrow's face. Kell knows the real one too well. Also, Harrow is cracked. Emotionally.
line.i.notAsMyself: As myself? He'd have me back in the cell before I finished my bow.
line.i.afterWarden: Off to the kitchen. Enjoy your supper, Kell. Now, the grate.
line.i.wallsLook: Ironhaven's walls, black against the snow.
line.i.sigridLook: An officer in a long coat, waiting in the snow. As if she knew I'd come out this door. Oh, I don't like that. I quite like that.
line.i.readSigrid: Nothing. She gives away nothing. How marvellous. How terrible.
dlgI.guard.wake1: Wha-? Sergeant Harrow! I wasn't asleep, sir! I was resting my eyes, sir!
dlgI.guard.wake2: Sir... how are you in the cell? The door's locked.
dlgI.guard.keysAsk: My keys, sir? But you've got your own ring... sir?
dlgI.guard.friend: Friend, sir? You've never called me that. Are you feeling all right, Sergeant?
dlgI.guard.scolded1: I'm sorry, Sergeant. It's the cold, sir. It gets into your bones down here.
dlgI.choice.warm: She won't hear it from me. Go up and warm yourself at the stove before you freeze. I'll finish the inspection.
dlgI.choice.report: Go and report to the captain. At once.
dlgI.guard.report: The captain? Sir, please. You always say you look out for your lads...
dlgI.guard.warm1: Really, sir? Thank you, sir! You're a good man, Sergeant, whatever they say about you.
dlgI.guard.warm2: Let me salute you proper, sir.
dlgI.choice.palm: Reach through the bars, clap his shoulder, and lift the key ring.
dlgI.guard.palmed: Thank you, sir! I won't forget it!
dlgI.choice.tally: Tally clerk. Quartermaster wants the night count. Your name's in his book, Kell.
dlgI.warden.passing: Nobody passes through here. Not at this hour.
dlgI.warden.orders: Harrow didn't say anything to me. And I know all Harrow's errand-boys.
dlgI.warden.tally1: The quartermaster? At this hour? ...What's he say about me?
dlgI.warden.tally2: Look, I'll pay him. Tell him I'll pay him.
dlgI.choice.kitchen: I'll count slowly. Long enough for a man to fetch his supper, say.
dlgI.choice.grate: Open the grate for me, would you?
dlgI.warden.grate: Open the grate? Why would a clerk need the grate?
dlgI.sigrid.1: The tally clerk doesn't come at night. And he's a head shorter than you.
dlgI.sigrid.2: Benn's upstairs, toasting his feet. He says Sergeant Harrow sent him. Harrow has been in Coppersong for a week.
dlgI.choice.clerk: Would you believe I'm a very tall clerk?
dlgI.choice.leaving: Captain! Lovely night for it. I was just leaving.
dlgI.sigrid.leaving: You were. Then you met me.
dlgI.sigrid.frame1: That frame under your hood. Brass, articulated. Who made it?
dlgI.sigrid.frame2: A friend made it for a theatre. I'm the only one who never took it off.
dlgI.sigrid.frame3: Out of bread, plaster and the wall of your own cell, you made a sergeant. I have a use for a man who can be anyone.
dlgI.sigrid.frame4: Walk with me. Before the real Harrow comes back from Coppersong.
hint.i.light.1: The moonlight from the window is thin. Something shiny could throw it further.
hint.i.light.2: Take the tin plate and use it on the window.
hint.i.frame.1: The frame lies on the guard's table, beyond reach. The cot might give a longer arm.
hint.i.frame.2: Take the nail and a strip from the cot, tie them together, and use the hook line on the table.
obj.i.face: Make a face the guard will obey.
hint.i.face.1: Who is the guard afraid of? The roster on the wall shows a face. The wall and the bucket give material.
hint.i.face.2: Look at the roster. Take plaster, wet it in the bucket, knead it with the crust, then use the putty on the frame.
hint.i.guard.1: Wear the mask and wake him. He'll have questions: how did his sergeant get into a locked cell, and where is the prisoner? What did you read in him?
hint.i.guard.2: Read the guard first. Then, as Harrow: say you locked yourself in to test him, that the prisoner was taken to the captain while he slept, and send him up to the stove.
hint.i.door.1: Keys, or something to pick the lock with.
hint.i.door.2: Use the key ring or the bent nail on the cell door.
hint.i.past.1: Kell knows Harrow. Someone else, then: there's a hood and a ledger here.
hint.i.past.2: Read Kell, take the hood and the ledger, put them together, wear the guise, and talk to him.
hint.i.grate.2: Once Kell is busy, use the bent nail on the grate.
note.i.guard: Benn: cold, tired, afraid of Sergeant Harrow. Snores in a minor key.
note.i.harrow: Harrow: heavy jaw, pouched eyes, broom moustache. Must practise the frown.
note.i.warden: Kell: hungry, bored, owes the quartermaster for dice. Three handles. I do love a handle.
diary.intro.cell: Woke in Ironhaven's cells wearing only my own face. Dreadful thing. I'll find a better one.
diary.intro.frame: Fished Nessa's frame off the guard's table with a nail and a strip of blanket. With the frame, I can be anyone. Anyone!
diary.intro.harrow: Made Sergeant Harrow out of bread and plaster. His own guard saluted him. I nearly saluted back.
diary.intro.clerk: Upstairs, a guard who knew Harrow too well. So I became nobody: a clerk with a ledger. Nobody is very restful.
diary.intro.sigrid: Captain Sigrid was waiting at the door. She saw straight through me, which never happens, and then offered me work. I think I'm in love. Or in trouble.
end.intro.text: Silas walks out of Ironhaven beside the captain who caught him. That is three days from now. The story starts where the cold does: in Cinderfold.
line.i.hookLine: Nail, meet string. I tie them together. A fishing line for a very small pond, with a very big fish.
dlgI.choice.lockedIn: I let myself in and locked it behind me, to see how long you'd sleep. Long enough, Benn.
dlgI.choice.moved: Taken up to the captain an hour ago. You slept through the whole transfer.
dlgI.guard.whatPrisoner: The thin one, sir. The one with the faces. You put him in here yourself...
dlgI.guard.underCot: Under the cot, sir? There's no room under that cot.
dlgI.guard.moved1: The captain? Oh no. She'll have my stripes for this. She'll have my ears.
dlgI.guard.moved2: What do I do, Sergeant? Please, sir. What do I do?
dlgI.choice.stay: Stay right where you are and don't move.
dlgI.guard.stay: Stay, sir? With you locked in the cell? Shouldn't I let you out?
line.i.dark.noPlate.1: I can't see a thing. Hello, darkness. You again.
line.i.dark.noPlate.2: Too dark. But something by my feet winked at me a moment ago. Cheeky.
line.i.dark.noPlate.3: Groping about blind. That glint on the floor by my feet... a plate? A plate! I do love a plate.
line.i.dark.plate.1: Still can't see. The only light on this side is that sliver of moon on the floor under the window. Lazy moon.
line.i.dark.plate.2: Dark, dark, dark. If only someone would carry that moonlight across the room for me...
line.i.dark.plate.3: The plate's dent is so shiny. Moon, meet plate. Plate, meet moon. Up at the window, the two of you.
